takeaways: Exchange Online starts with default settings, so mail flow, anti-spam, anti-phishing and anti-malware still need to be configured for the organization's needs.
Identity security comes first: protect every user and service account, use PIM for Exchange admins and secure break glass accounts with FIDO keys.
Configure SPF, DKIM and DMARC with real policies, use subdomains for third-party senders, and enable Safe Links in Defender for Office 365.
hook: Many Microsoft messaging environments look secure on the surface but still run on defaults, weak identities and misunderstood mail flow. This conversation with Exchange MVP Thomas Stensitzki is for Exchange and Microsoft 365 administrators running on-premises, hybrid or cloud-only email. It covers identity protection, break glass accounts, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, Defender for Office 365 and the operational discipline that keeps messaging secure.
